intro: G-code to image draws a G-code's extrusion toolpaths seen from above: of a specific layer, to check the infill, perimeters or a problem area, or of all of them at once, coloured from bottom to top, for a preview of the job without opening the slicer.

Only moves that extrude are drawn; travel moves without plastic and retractions are ignored. Choose the layer by its number (the result note says its height and how many there are) or 0 for all, and the format: PNG at the size you want or vector SVG in millimetres, which can be enlarged without losing detail or printed to scale.

It accepts G-code from any slicer and Prusa bgcode. It is useful to document a job, share how a layer looks on a forum or check that the G-code you are about to send is the one you think. To see the part in 3D, use the G-code viewer.
You can process up to ten files per task. They are processed on our server in the European Union and deleted automatically when they expire.

faq.q: How do I know which layer number I want?
faq.a: First generate the image of all layers: the note says how many there are; 1 is the first.
Yes, everything that is extruded, in the colour of its height.

faq.q: Why is the SVG so heavy?
faq.a: Because each segment is a line; for very long G-code, PNG is lighter.

faq.q: Can I see the first layer?
faq.a: Yes: choose layer 1 to check adhesion and the brim before printing.
From blue for the bottom layers to red for the top ones, to tell heights apart.
